Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice S.R.Krishna Kumar
 Oral Order

In this petition, the petitioners seeks the following reliefs:
"(a) To quash the entire proceedings in C.C.No.10825/2017 on the file of the XXX Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.
(b) Pass such other order or orders as this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the facts and circumstances of the case in the interest of justice and equity."

entities.text: XXX Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the material on record.
3.

A perusal of the material on record will indicate that respondent No.2-complainant filed a complaint before respondent No.1 police in Crime No.399/2017, which culminated in C.C.No.10825/2017 before the Trial Court, punishable for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 324, 506, 109 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

Further, the matrimonial dispute between petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 in Civil Petition No.3/2019 before the Family Court, Cuttack, ended up in settlement, wherein both parties settled NC:
2025:KHC:24854 HC-KAR the matrimonial dispute with mutual consent and further agreed to co-operate for quashing of criminal proceedings pending before the Trial Court.

The relevant portion of the Application filed under Order 23 Rule 3 CPC, filed before the Family Court, Cuttack,
reads as under:
"(H) That within the said 75 days from the date of order, the Petitioner No1. shall withdraw all the Criminal Cases like D.V. Case, G.R. Cases pending before different courts initiated by the petitioner No.1 against the petitioner No.2 making free the husband (Petitioner No.2) from its all criminal liabilities."
Sri. Jagannath Ojha vs State Of Karnataka on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26223719/
3 4.

entities.text: Jagannath Ojha vs State Of Karnataka on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances and the fact that the petitioner No.1-accused and respondent No.2- complainant have settled the matrimonial dispute and also agreed to co-operate for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.10825/2017 pending before the Trial Court,
continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners would amount to abuse of process of law and the same deserves to be quashed.
5. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The petition is allowed.

NC: 2025:KHC:24854 HC-KAR ii) The impugned criminal proceedings in C.C.No.10825/2017 (arising out of Crime No.399/2017 registered by respondent No.1- Police), pending on the file of the XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, in so far as the petitioners are concerned, are hereby quashed.
